novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new phenomenon/mechanistic relationship—“reasoning LLMs spend MORE internal reasoning effort ... constructing a strategically deceptive answer” and that the “deception-effort surplus GROWS when the prompt signals the lie is likely to be detected”—rather than merely a new detector; its measurement route is a pre-answer compute-allocation signal separable from difficulty and honesty. The closest prior work I found is “When Thinking LLMs Lie: Unveiling the Strategic Deception in Representations of Reasoning Models” and “Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models”; searches using “LLM deception reasoning effort,” “detectability belief deception compute,” “deception chain-of-thought length,” “evaluation awareness activation steering,” and “strategic dishonesty internal representations” found work on whether models deceive and how deception/evaluation-awareness directions can be decoded or steered, but not this detectability-conditioned effort-cost relationship. The step from those works to this claim requires a new core relationship—deception versus honesty in internal reasoning effort moderated by perceived detectability—although the proposed probing, patching, and steering techniques are largely natural extensions of representation-engineering practice, warranting high but not paradigm-level novelty.
